analysis.answer: Current law has no provisions addressing religious displays in public school classrooms. The measure explicitly requires every public school classroom to display an 11-by-14-inch poster of the Five Pillars of Islam.
Public school districts, individual schools, or teachers will bear the direct costs of acquiring, printing, or purchasing the required posters for every classroom.
Schools or teachers will likely bear the financial burden of providing the posters. Members of the Islamic faith may benefit from seeing their religion prominently represented in public spaces.

Schools will need to obtain and install the posters to comply. The mandate may face legal challenges regarding the constitutional separation of religion and state, which could lead to court injunctions blocking its enforcement.
The text asserts no specific problem. Its mechanism directly alters the visual environment of classrooms by mandating the display of the Five Pillars of Islam.
The text strictly requires the display in every classroom, leaving little to no discretion for local school boards, administrators, or teachers to opt out.
Enforcement mechanisms are not specified, so administrative costs would depend on how districts choose to monitor and ensure compliance across all classrooms.
Assuming it is a statutory measure, it could be repealed or amended by a future legislative vote, or it could be overturned by the courts if found unconstitutional.

flags.quote: Each public school classroom shall display a poster of the Five Pillars of Islam
